summary.text: A cyclic group is a group generated by a single element, so every other element comes from repeatedly applying the operation to that generator or its inverse.
Every cyclic group is abelian, meaning its group operation is commutative.
The integers Z under addition form an infinite cyclic group, and the integers modulo n under addition form a finite one, Z/nZ.

facts.label: Generator
facts.value: One element g whose powers or multiples give every element

facts.label: Integer generators
facts.value: In the integers under addition, only 1 and −1 generate

facts.label: Prime order
facts.value: A cyclic group of prime order is simple

facts.label: Polygon rotations
facts.value: A polygon's rotational symmetries form a finite cyclic group

facts.label: Not cyclic
facts.value: The group of all rotations of a circle

items.prompt: In the integers modulo 6 under addition, which element can build the whole group by repeated addition?
items.explain: An element generates the group when it is relatively prime to n; 5 is relatively prime to 6, while 2, 3 and 4 are not.

items.prompt: Which numbers can generate the integers under addition by repeated adding and subtracting?

options.label: Every positive integer
Only 1 and −1
Only 1
Every odd integer

items.explain: All integers can be built from 1, and 1 and −1 are the only generators.

items.prompt: In a cyclic group you combine two elements a and b. Can the order of combining change the result?

options.label: Yes, ab and ba usually differ
Yes, but only in infinite cyclic groups
No, the operation is commutative
No, but only for prime order

items.explain: Every cyclic group is abelian, so its operation is commutative.

items.prompt: A regular polygon can be moved onto itself by n different rotations, counting the do-nothing rotation. What group do these form?

options.label: A group that is not abelian
The group of all circle rotations
A finite field
A cyclic group of n elements

items.explain: The rotational symmetries of a polygon form a finite cyclic group isomorphic to Z/nZ.

items.prompt: Why is the group of all rotations of a circle not cyclic?

options.label: No single rotation has powers that give every rotation
Rotations do not combine to give a rotation
A circle has too few symmetries
Its operation is not commutative

items.explain: A cyclic group needs one generator whose integer powers produce everything, and no single rotation does that for all rotations of a circle.

items.prompt: A cyclic group has a prime number of elements. What special property follows?

options.label: It cannot be a commutative group
It has no single generator at all
It must be an infinite group
It cannot be broken into smaller groups

items.explain: A cyclic group of prime order is simple, so it cannot be broken down into smaller groups.
